interactions.label: A 25-year-old primigravida is assessed during an antenatal visit. Pelvic examina

params.question: A 25-year-old primigravida is assessed during an antenatal visit. Pelvic examination reveals prominent ischial spines, converging sidewalls, and a narrow sub-pubic arch. Which pelvic type does this examination suggest?

answers.text: Gynecoid

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A gynecoid pelvis has straight sidewalls, a wide sub-pubic arch, and a round inlet — none of which match these findings.

answers.text: Android

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The android pelvis is characterised by prominent ischial spines, converging (funnel-shaped) sidewalls, a narrow sub-pubic arch, and a heart-shaped inlet. It predisposes to posterior positions and mid-pelvis arrest.

answers.text: Anthropoid

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The anthropoid pelvis has a long anteroposterior diameter with straight sidewalls, not the converging pattern described here.

answers.text: Platypelloid

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The platypelloid pelvis is flat and wide with widely spaced ischial spines — the opposite of prominent spines with converging sidewalls.

overallFeedback.feedback: The combination of prominent ischial spines, converging sidewalls, and a narrow sub-pubic arch is the hallmark of the android pelvis (~25% of women). Clinically, this shape predisposes to posterior positions and arrest at the mid-pelvis.
Well done. The android pelvis has a classic triad — prominent spines, converging sidewalls, and a narrow sub-pubic arch — and carries a higher risk of deep transverse arrest.

interactions.label: During labour, the foetal head tucks the chin toward the chest as it descends th

params.question: During labour, the foetal head tucks the chin toward the chest as it descends through the mid-pelvis. What is the primary purpose of this movement (flexion)?

answers.text: To align the occiput with the anteroposterior diameter of the pelvic outlet

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Alignment with the outlet's anteroposterior diameter occurs during internal rotation, not flexion. Flexion changes which diameter of the skull is presented.

answers.text: To present the smallest possible diameter of the foetal head to the pelvis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Flexion substitutes the smaller suboccipitobregmatic diameter for the larger occipitofrontal diameter, allowing the head to negotiate the narrower mid-pelvis.

answers.text: To facilitate engagement of the biparietal diameter at the pelvic inlet

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Engagement occurs before significant flexion and involves the biparietal diameter passing through the pelvic inlet, not the mid-pelvis.

answers.text: To prepare the head for external rotation after delivery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: External rotation (restitution) occurs after the head is delivered and realigns with the shoulders — it is not the purpose of flexion during descent.

overallFeedback.feedback: Flexion tucks the chin toward the chest, replacing the larger occipitofrontal diameter with the smaller suboccipitobregmatic diameter. This diameter reduction is what allows the head to pass through the narrow mid-pelvis.
Well done. Flexion is a diameter-reducing manoeuvre — the head tucks to present its smallest circumference, making the tight fit through the mid-pelvis possible.

interactions.label: On a WHO partograph, a primigravida's cervical dilatation plot has just crossed

params.question: On a WHO partograph, a primigravida's cervical dilatation plot has just crossed the action line. Analysing this finding, which of the following best explains its clinical significance?

answers.text: The rate of cervical dilatation has exceeded the expected 1 cm per hour

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: If dilatation exceeded 1 cm/hour, the plot would remain to the LEFT of the alert line. Crossing the action line indicates the opposite — progress is dangerously slow.

answers.text: Labour progress has fallen more than four hours behind the minimum expected rate

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The action line sits four hours to the right of the alert line. Crossing it means progress has stalled more than four hours beyond the minimum acceptable rate, mandating immediate obstetric review.

answers.text: The foetal heart rate tracing has become non-reassuring

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Foetal heart rate is recorded in a separate section of the partograph (foetal condition section), not on the cervicograph where the alert and action lines appear.

answers.text: Meconium-stained liquor has been detected during labour

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Liquor colour is documented in the foetal condition section of the partograph, not the cervicograph. The action line relates solely to the rate of cervical dilatation.

overallFeedback.feedback: The action line is drawn four hours to the right of the alert line on the cervicograph. When the dilatation plot reaches it, labour has stalled more than four hours beyond the minimum expected rate — this requires immediate obstetric review.

Well done. The action line, positioned four hours to the right of the alert line, signals dangerously slow progress and requires immediate senior obstetric review for possible augmentation or caesarean section.

interactions.label: A clinician is about to perform artificial rupture of membranes. The foetal head

params.question: A clinician is about to perform artificial rupture of membranes. The foetal head is unengaged and floating above the pelvic inlet. What is the most serious immediate risk of proceeding with amniotomy?

answers.text: Chorioamnionitis from prolonged membrane rupture

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Infection risk increases with time after rupture but develops over hours. The most immediate danger with an unengaged head is an acute emergency that can occur within seconds of rupture.

answers.text: Umbilical cord prolapse

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. When the presenting part is not well applied to the cervix, the rush of amniotic fluid during amniotomy can sweep a loop of umbilical cord through the cervix — a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate caesarean section.

answers.text: Premature separation of the placenta

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Placental abruption is not directly caused by amniotomy. The principal risk when the head is unengaged is cord prolapse, because the presenting part does not seal the cervix.

answers.text: Uterine rupture from sudden decompression

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Uterine rupture is associated with obstructed labour or previous caesarean scars, not with amniotomy. The key risk with an unengaged head is cord prolapse.

overallFeedback.feedback: The most serious risk of performing ARM with an unengaged head is cord prolapse. Without the head sealing the cervix, amniotic fluid rushes out and can carry a loop of umbilical cord through — this is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate caesarean delivery.
Well done. Without an engaged presenting part sealing the cervix, the sudden rush of fluid during amniotomy can sweep the cord ahead of the head — cord prolapse demands emergency caesarean section.

interactions.label: A final-year student measures a diagonal conjugate of 11 cm on vaginal examinati

params.question: A final-year student measures a diagonal conjugate of 11 cm on vaginal examination. After subtracting 1.5 cm, the estimated obstetric conjugate is 9.5 cm. Which of the following best justifies the appropriate management?

answers.text: The measurements are within normal limits; routine antenatal care is sufficient

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An obstetric conjugate of 9.5 cm is below the normal threshold of approximately 10 cm. This indicates a contracted inlet that warrants further evaluation during labour.

answers.text: The inlet is contracted; an elective caesarean section should be planned

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pelvic measurements alone do not determine the mode of delivery. Factors such as foetal size, moulding capacity, and uterine contractile force all contribute — a trial of labour is the definitive test.

answers.text: The inlet is contracted; a trial of labour with close monitoring is the appropriate test of pelvic adequacy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. An obstetric conjugate of 9.5 cm indicates a contracted inlet. A trial of labour — not X-ray pelvimetry — remains the true test of whether the foetal head can negotiate the pelvis, because it accounts for moulding and soft tissue factors that static measurements cannot capture.

answers.text: X-ray pelvimetry should be ordered to confirm the exact measurement before deciding

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A trial of labour, not X-ray pelvimetry, is the true test of pelvic adequacy. Static imaging cannot predict the dynamic interaction between the foetal head and the birth canal during labour.

overallFeedback.feedback: An obstetric conjugate of 9.5 cm (diagonal conjugate 11 cm minus 1.5 cm) indicates a contracted inlet. The key principle is that a trial of labour — not X-ray pelvimetry — is the definitive test of pelvic adequacy, because it accounts for moulding and uterine forces that static measurements miss.
Well done. A 9.5 cm obstetric conjugate is contracted, but the definitive test of pelvic adequacy is a trial of labour with careful monitoring — not imaging or automatic operative delivery.
